True Statement: An ecosystem consists of biotic components comprising living organisms and abiotic components comprising physical factors like temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals.
False 1: An ecosystem consists of biotic components comprising living organisms and abiotic components comprising only living factors like plants and animals.

True Statement: Natural ecosystems include forests, ponds and lakes, while gardens and crop-fields are human-made (artificial) ecosystems.
False 1: Natural ecosystems include gardens and crop-fields, while forests, ponds and lakes are human-made (artificial) ecosystems.

True Statement: Green plants and certain bacteria that produce food by photosynthesis are called producers.
False 1: Green plants and certain bacteria that produce food by photosynthesis are called consumers.
False 2: Animals that consume food produced by other organisms are called producers.

True Statement: Consumers are organisms that consume food produced either directly from producers or indirectly by feeding on other consumers.
False 1: Producers are organisms that consume food produced either directly from other producers or indirectly by feeding on other consumers.

True Statement: Microorganisms comprising bacteria and fungi break down the dead remains and waste products of organisms and are called decomposers.
False 1: Microorganisms comprising bacteria and fungi break down the dead remains and waste products of organisms and are called producers.
False 2: Microorganisms comprising bacteria and fungi break down the dead remains and waste products of organisms and are called consumers.

True Statement: Decomposers break down complex organic substances into simple inorganic substances that go into the soil and are used up once more by plants.
False 1: Decomposers break down simple inorganic substances into complex organic substances that go into the soil and are used up once more by plants.

True Statement: Each step or level of the food chain forms a trophic level.
False 1: Each step or level of the food chain forms a feeding level.

True Statement: Autotrophs or producers are at the first trophic level; they fix solar energy and make it available for heterotrophs or consumers.
False 1: Heterotrophs or consumers are at the first trophic level; they fix solar energy and make it available for autotrophs or producers.

True Statement: Herbivores or primary consumers come at the second trophic level.
False 1: Herbivores or primary consumers come at the first trophic level.
False 2: Carnivores or secondary consumers come at the second trophic level.

True Statement: Small carnivores or secondary consumers are at the third trophic level, and larger carnivores or tertiary consumers form the fourth trophic level.
False 1: Small carnivores or secondary consumers are at the fourth trophic level, and larger carnivores or tertiary consumers form the third trophic level.

True Statement: Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about 1% of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.
False 1: Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about 10% of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.

True Statement: An average of 10% of the food eaten by organisms is turned into their own body mass and made available for the next level of consumers.
False 1: An average of 50% of the food eaten by organisms is turned into their own body mass and made available for the next level of consumers.

True Statement: Food chains generally consist of only three or four steps because so little energy is available for the next level of consumers.
False 1: Food chains generally consist of only ten or more steps because so little energy is available for the next level of consumers.

True Statement: There are generally a greater number of individuals at the lower trophic levels of an ecosystem, with the greatest number being the producers.
False 1: There are generally a greater number of individuals at the higher trophic levels of an ecosystem, with the greatest number being the top carnivores.

True Statement: A food web is a series of branching lines showing that each organism is generally eaten by two or more other kinds of organisms.
False 1: A food web is a straight-line chain showing that each organism is eaten by exactly one other organism.

True Statement: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is unidirectional: energy captured by autotrophs does not revert back to the solar input.
False 1: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is bidirectional: energy captured by autotrophs can revert back to the solar input.

True Statement: The energy available at each trophic level gets diminished progressively due to loss of energy at each level.
False 1: The energy available at each trophic level increases progressively due to accumulation of energy at each level.

True Statement: Harmful chemicals like pesticides that are not degradable get accumulated progressively at each trophic level; this is known as biological magnification.
False 1: Harmful chemicals like pesticides that are not degradable get equally distributed across all trophic levels; this is known as biological magnification.
False 2: Beneficial nutrients get accumulated progressively at each trophic level; this is known as biological magnification.

True Statement: As human beings occupy the top level in any food chain, the maximum concentration of pesticide chemicals gets accumulated in our bodies.
False 1: As human beings occupy the top level in any food chain, the minimum concentration of pesticide chemicals gets accumulated in our bodies.

True Statement: Ozone (O₃) is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen.
False 1: Ozone (O₃) is a molecule formed by two atoms of oxygen.
False 2: Ozone (O₃) is a molecule formed by four atoms of oxygen.

True Statement: Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.
False 1: Ozone at the lower levels of the atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.
False 2: Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from infrared radiation from the Sun.

True Statement: UV radiation is known to cause skin cancer in human beings.
False 1: UV radiation is known to cause lung cancer in human beings.

True Statement: Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere is a product of UV radiation acting on oxygen (O₂) molecules to produce free oxygen atoms, which then combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.
False 1: Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere is a product of infrared radiation acting on oxygen (O₂) molecules to produce free oxygen atoms, which then combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.

True Statement: The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s, linked to synthetic chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.
False 1: The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s, linked to synthetic chemicals like nitrogen oxides used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.
False 2: The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to increase sharply in the 1980s, linked to synthetic chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.

True Statement: In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) succeeded in forging an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels.
False 1: In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) succeeded in forging an agreement to ban CFC production entirely.

True Statement: Substances that are broken down by biological processes are said to be biodegradable.
False 1: Substances that are broken down by biological processes are said to be non-biodegradable.

True Statement: Non-biodegradable substances may be inert and persist in the environment for a long time, or may harm the various members of the ecosystem.
False 1: Non-biodegradable substances are quickly broken down and do not harm the members of the ecosystem.
